court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
case_name: Vasant Ramchandra Alias Chander ... vs Gurudas Vasantrao Yelvande And Ors on 16 April, 2018

legal_principles.principle: A child born out of a void marriage is legitimate and can claim a share in the property of their parents.
legal_principles.held: Notwithstanding that marriage is null and void, any child of such marriage who would have been legitimate if the marriage had been valid, shall be legitimate.

legal_principles.principle: A child born out of a voidable marriage can claim a share in the property of their parents, but only through succession.
legal_principles.held: Where a decree of nullity is granted in respect of a voidable marriage under section 12, any child begotten or conceived before the decree is made, who would have been the legitimate child of the parties to the marriage if at the date of the decree it had been dissolved instead of being annulled, shall be deemed to be their legitimate child notwithstanding the decree of nullity.

legal_principles.principle: A child born out of a void or voidable marriage cannot claim a share in the joint family property.
legal_principles.held: In our opinion, therefore, it will be incorrect to say that, the son of a void marriage, though legitimate by virtue of the provisions contained in Section 16 of the Hindu Marriage Act, can claim a share in the property, which belongs to a coparcenary, of which his father is a Member.
cited_cases: Shantaram Tukaram Patil and Anr. Vs. Smt. Dagubai Tukaram Patil and Ors., (1987) Bom.C.R. 714

legal_principles.principle: A child born out of a void or voidable marriage can only claim their share in the property during the lifetime of their father.
legal_principles.held: Whether such children claim their share in the property during the lifetime of their father?

use_for_drafting: assisting in joint family settlement negotiations
